# **Comparative Architectural and Algorithmic Analysis for Melody-to-Accompaniment Symbolic Music Generation on POP909**

## **1\. Small-Data From-Scratch Recipes for Melody-to-Piano Accompaniment**

Training Transformer models from scratch on small symbolic music corpora—such as the POP909 dataset containing 896 training songs (\~60 hours of multi-track Mandopop piano arrangements)—presents severe optimization challenges1. When external pre-trained weights and supplementary datasets are prohibited, standard autoregressive sequence models quickly memorize training distributions, leading to attention collapse and high validation perplexity3. To mitigate these issues, symbolic Music Information Retrieval (MIR) literature emphasizes specialized event representations, structural factorizations, and aggressive data augmentation to stabilize optimization under constrained data regimes5.

| System / Model | Primary Tokenization | Dataset & Size | Architecture & Parameters | Augmentation & Training Recipe | Reported Objective Metrics |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **PopMAG** \[cite: 5, 8\] | MuMIDI (Interleaved track, position, note, chord)8 | \~14k pop songs (LMD / FreeMidi / CPMD)5 | Recurrent Transformer Enc-Dec with bar embeddings8 | Teacher forcing, bar/position embeddings, 32 timesteps/bar8 | **Chord Accuracy (CA)**: ![][image1] \[cite: 9\] |
| **Compose & Embellish** \[cite: 6, 10\] | REMI / REMI+ (Track, Bar, Tempo, Pitch, Vel, Dur)6 | Pop1K7 (1,591 songs) & LMD-full (14,934 songs)6 | Two-stage: ![][image2] Lead Sheet \+ ![][image3] Performance Model6 | Linear Transformer / GPT-like decoder, phrase-level crops6 | **Pitch H1/H4**: Reduced structural gap by 50% vs SOTA6 |
| **Anticipatory Music Transformer** \[cite: 7, 13\] | Arrival-Time Encoding (Onset, Duration, Note, Rest)7 | Lakh MIDI (\~170k songs)14 | GPT-2 style causal Transformer (360M params)7 | Interleaved control/event process, anticipation window ![][image4] \[cite: 7\] | **NLL / Event Loss**: Lower perplexity with anticipation7 |
| **SymPAC** \[cite: 15\] | REMI \+ Chord & Section Control Tokens15 | Auto-transcribed & Symbolic Corpora15 | Causal LM with Finite State Machine (FSM) constraints15 | Prompt-bar encoding, grammar-constrained decoding15 | **Overlapped Area (OA)**: Up to 40% improvement on attributes16 |

Quantitative evaluation of generated accompaniments against ground-truth piano tracks requires measuring harmonic alignment and statistical distribution similarity1. Chord Accuracy (CA) measures per-bar harmonic fidelity by estimating the generated piano's dominant triad via bass-weighted chroma cosine similarity1. For a given bar ![][image5], the pitch-class chroma vector ![][image6] aggregates active note pitch classes while applying a ![][image7] weight multiplier to the lowest pitch active within the bar1:  
![][image8]  
The estimated chord ![][image9] is identified by finding the candidate triad vector ![][image10] across 24 major and minor triads that maximizes cosine similarity:  
![][image11]  
Chord Accuracy reflects the percentage of evaluable bars where ![][image9] matches the ground-truth chord label1. Bars designated as diminished, augmented, suspended, or unannotated (![][image12]) are omitted from evaluation, establishing an empirical CA-ceiling bounded by human performance on ground-truth piano tracks1.  
Overlapped Area (OA) measures the similarity between Kernel Density Estimation (KDE) smoothed distributions of generated and target piano attributes1. For an attribute ![][image13], continuous density estimates ![][image14] and ![][image15] yield an overlap score defined as1:  
![][image16]  
Training effectively on POP909's 896 songs requires specific dataset preparation techniques1. Pitch transposition augmentation shifts every 16-bar training pair across all 12 chromatic keys (![][image17] semitones), expanding the training corpus twelvefold to 10,752 samples18. This step forces scale invariance and reduces key-specific memorization18. Additionally, sliding-window bar cropping with a stride of 2 or 4 bars introduces dynamic phrase boundaries during training, mitigating positional biases16. Using a 16th-note REMI-like tokenization scheme (pos\_per\_beat=4) with event ordering (Pos\_x, Pitch\_x, Vel\_x, Dur\_x) maintains a compact vocabulary of ![][image18] tokens1. On POP909, an average melody bar yields ![][image19] notes (16 tokens) and a piano bar yields ![][image20] notes (52 tokens), generating a total 16-bar sequence length of ![][image21] tokens1.

## **2\. Interleaving Design for Decoder-Only Conditional Generation**

Decoder-only architectures frame conditional accompaniment generation as sequence modeling over a unified token stream1. Achieving structural alignment between the conditioning melody track ![][image22] and the generated piano track ![][image23] depends on sequence layout, lookahead exposure, and target loss masking1.  
Bar-level interleaving formats sequences into alternating bar blocks (\<M\_bar\_k\> \<P\_bar\_k\>), preserving intra-bar coherence while allowing self-attention layers to learn cross-track dependencies within local time steps1. Beat-level interleaving alternates tracks at beat boundaries (\<M\_beat\_b\> \<P\_beat\_b\>), which increases track-switch token overhead and fragments sustained notes8. Event-level arrival-time interleaving sorts events from both processes along a continuous timeline based on onset timestamps ![][image24]7. Using an anticipation operator ![][image25], control and melody tokens are shifted forward by an anticipation interval ![][image26], forcing the model to attend to upcoming control events before outputting present musical notes7.  
In bar-interleaved causal decoders, lookahead defines the number of future melody bars exposed to the model before generating the current piano bar1. Synchronous generation (Lookahead 0\) orders sequences as \<M\_1\> \<P\_1\> \<M\_2\> \<P\_2\>, forcing the model to predict ![][image27] using only current and past melody context ![][image28]1. This deprives the architecture of context regarding impending harmonic resolutions20. Exposing a 1-bar lookahead (\<M\_1\> \<M\_2\> \<P\_1\> \<M\_3\> \<P\_2\>) allows the model to inspect ![][image29] while generating ![][image27]1. This approach mirrors human accompaniment practices, where musicians look ahead to prepare harmonic transitions and voice-leading figures6. Expanding lookahead to 2 or more bars exposes broader context, but increases sequence length and can cause self-attention layers to underattend to immediate rhythmic alignment4.  
During training, cross-entropy loss must be masked to evaluate exclusively on target piano tokens (![][image23])7. Zeroing loss gradients on conditioning melody tokens (![][image22]) ensures model parameters directly optimize ![][image30]7. Computing loss on conditioning tokens wastes capacity on predicting known prompt tokens, degrading accompaniment generation7.  
At inference, forced-condition decoding inputs ground-truth melody tokens from unseen test prompts while sampling piano tokens autoregressively1. This setup introduces exposure bias, where minor generation errors in early piano bars accumulate over time, leading to degraded note density or unexpected silence8. Additionally, unconstrained sampling can cause the model to emit track-switching control tokens (\<M\>) prematurely, breaking sequence formatting15. To prevent sequence corruption, logit masking must be enforced during piano generation passes, suppressing melody and track header tokens to ![][image31] until a deterministic bar-end token is reached15.

## **3\. T5/BART-Style Encoder-Decoder Architectures on Small Datasets**

Sequence-to-sequence encoder-decoder models decouple prompt processing from target sequence generation1. The encoder processes the full 16-bar melody prompt (![][image32] tokens) bidirectionally, while the decoder causally generates the 16-bar piano accompaniment (![][image33] tokens) through cross-attention mechanisms1.  
Standard T5 implementations use relative position bias matrices rather than absolute positional embeddings23. Relative distances ![][image34] between query ![][image35] and key ![][image36] are mapped into logarithmic parameter buckets defined by relative\_attention\_num\_buckets (default 32\) and relative\_attention\_max\_distance (default 128\)23. In symbolic music generation, where 16-bar sequences extend from 1,000 to 2,000 tokens, any relative distance exceeding 128 tokens collapses into the final parameter bucket23. This prevents the decoder from distinguishing whether a note occurred 150 or 800 tokens prior, causing position smearing and loss of structural bar index awareness across long sequences4. To address this issue when training from scratch, relative\_attention\_num\_buckets should be expanded to 64 or 128, relative\_attention\_max\_distance increased to 512 or 1024, and explicit bar position tokens (Bar\_1 ... Bar\_16) prepended to the token stream8.

| Parameter | Standard T5-Small Default | Recommended Small-Data Recipe (\<1k Songs) | Technical Justification |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| d\_model / d\_kv | 512 / 64 | 256 / 32 | Reduces model capacity to prevent memorization on 896 songs3. |
| num\_layers (Enc/Dec) | 6 / 6 | 4 / 4 | Mitigates gradient vanishing in uninitialized cross-attention blocks22. |
| num\_heads | 8 | 4 or 8 | Maintains head dimension ![][image37] or ![][image38]. |
| dropout\_rate | 0.10 | 0.15–0.20 | Increases regularization against dataset-specific pitch patterns24. |
| weight\_decay | 0.00 | 0.01–0.10 | Penalizes large embedding and projection weights. |
| learning\_rate | ![][image39] | ![][image40] (AdamW) | Linear warmup over 1,000 steps with cosine decay prevents early divergence. |
| tie\_word\_embeddings | True | False | Encoder and decoder use distinct vocabulary distributions1. |
| Precision | fp32 | bfloat16 | Prevents underflow during Softmax calculations while preserving dynamic range. |

Architecturally, decoder-only models (GPT-2) demonstrate higher sample efficiency than encoder-decoder models (T5) when trained from scratch on small datasets1. Shared self-attention layers in decoder-only setups process melody and accompaniment within a single representation space, learning cross-track correlations directly1. Conversely, encoder-decoder models rely on cross-attention modules to connect unaligned encoder and decoder representations, which struggle to converge without pre-training on large corpora3. While T5 supports global melody context out of the box through bidirectional encoding, decoder-only architectures achieve similar contextual access more reliably via structured bar-interleaving with lookahead windows1.

## **4\. Harmony Control Mechanics**

Maintaining harmonic consistency between conditioning melodies and generated accompaniments is essential in symbolic music generation5. Models trained on small corpora without explicit harmonic guidance often generate non-harmonic tones or incoherent chord progressions5.  
Inserting explicit per-bar chord tokens (e.g., Chord\_C:maj) into the conditioning sequence establishes a clear harmonic template8. Utilizing a vocabulary of 84 chord classes (12 roots ![][image41] 7 chord types), this approach elevates Chord Accuracy (CA) to ![][image42]8. However, if the task requires pure melody-to-piano generation without auxiliary harmonic inputs, extracting chords from evaluation files (chord\_midi.txt) introduces test-set data leakage.  
Training models to predict an interleaved chord token before generating piano bar notes (\<M\_bar\_k\> \<P\_bar\_k\_Chord\> \<P\_bar\_k\_Notes\>) forces intermediate hidden states to perform an implicit harmonic estimation task8. This structural requirement improves internal harmonic consistency, raising CA by ![][image43] over unconditioned baselines without relying on privileged external annotations at test time8.  
Adding an auxiliary multi-class chord classification loss ![][image44] to intermediate representations acts as an effective regularizer during training27:  
![][image45]  
This objective penalizes pitch predictions that deviate from the root triad of the annotated bar27. Because the auxiliary loss operates only during parameter updates, it leaves inference latency unaffected27.  
Guided decoding uses Finite State Machines (FSMs) or dynamic logit masks to enforce harmonic constraints at test time15. Modifying predicted pitch logits with a mask vector ![][image46] suppresses out-of-key pitch classes15:  
![][image47]  
This mechanism prevents out-of-key dissonance and ensures scale adherence using decoding rules derived directly from the input melody prompt15.  
Best-of\-![][image12] sampling generates ![][image12] candidate accompaniments (![][image48]) for a given melody prompt using standard autoregressive sampling1. Each candidate is evaluated using the target evaluation metric—computing bass-weighted chroma cosine similarity against inferred bar chords—and the top-scoring candidate is selected1. This inference procedure recovers from localized autoregressive generation errors, yielding gains in evaluation CA (+0.12–0.20) without modifying model architectures or inputs1.

## **5\. Inference-Time Algorithmic Enhancements**

Tailoring inference decoding strategies allows models to maximize objective performance metrics without retraining parameters1.  
Applying distinct sampling parameters across token types aligns generation with the structure of symbolic music sequences1. Position tokens (Pos\_x) benefit from low temperatures (![][image49], ![][image50]) to enforce a strict 16th-note rhythmic grid and prevent timing drift1. Pitch tokens (Pitch\_x) perform best with moderate temperatures (![][image51], ![][image52]), balancing harmonic precision with pitch variety7. Velocity tokens (Vel\_x) use higher sampling settings (![][image53], ![][image54]) to encourage dynamic expression11. Duration tokens (Dur\_x) require lower temperatures (![][image55], ![][image56]) to prevent unnatural note overlaps and muddy textures1.  
Standard token repetition penalties applied uniformly across symbolic music representations degrade output quality by penalizing necessary position and duration tokens11. Restricting repetition penalties to pitch tokens (Pitch\_x) resolves this issue11. For candidate pitch tokens ![][image57] within a recent pitch context window ![][image58] of size ![][image59], adjusting logits via:  
![][image60]  
using ![][image61] breaks repetitive pitch loops while preserving underlying rhythmic patterns16.  
When key signatures are known or estimated using key-finding algorithms, adding a key-aware logit bias vector ![][image62] before Softmax calculation reinforces tonal stability18. Assigning positive biases to scale degrees (![][image63]) and penalizing non-harmonic tones (![][image64]) suppresses out-of-key dissonance and raises Chord Accuracy while preserving valid chromatic passes18.

## **6\. Unconditional Task Optimization Levers**

The unconditional task requires generating 32-bar pop piano compositions without prompting1. Models are evaluated against ground-truth statistical distributions using three primary metrics1:

* **H1**: 1-Bar Pitch-Class Entropy, measuring short-term tonal diversity6.  
* **H4**: 4-Bar Pitch-Class Entropy, measuring phrase-level tonal diversity6.  
* **GS**: Grooving Pattern Similarity, measuring rhythmic matrix cosine similarity across consecutive 4-bar blocks6. High GS scores indicate structured rhythmic grooves, while low scores signal erratic timing6.

Reference values measured on POP909 32-bar crops are ![][image69], ![][image70], and ![][image71]1.  
Overtraining small models on POP909 leads to distribution collapse4. As cross-entropy training progresses past optimal validation perplexity, model confidence becomes excessively sharp4. This causes H1 and H4 entropy metrics to drop below target levels (![][image72]) while GS spikes toward ![][image73] due to repetitive looping4. Halting training at minimal validation perplexity preserves pitch entropy, keeping H1 and H4 aligned with real-data reference targets6.  
Incorporating label smoothing (![][image74]) during cross-entropy training prevents probability mass from concentrating on dominant pitch classes7:  
![][image75]  
This regularization prevents overconfident predictions, raising low H1 and H4 scores toward target reference values (![][image76] and ![][image77])1.  
Generating 32-bar piano sequences requires handling context lengths of ![][image78] to ![][image79] tokens1. Standard absolute learned positional embeddings struggle to maintain structural cohesion across these lengths, leading to late-sequence rhythmic breakdown4. Modern positional schemes such as Rotary Position Embeddings (RoPE) or ALiBi preserve relative distance awareness across ![][image79] tokens, stabilizing long-range structure and maintaining target GS levels (![][image80])1.  
Sampling parameter selection directly influences generated entropy7. Increasing top\-![][image81] (![][image82]) or temperature (![][image83]) expands output diversity, increasing H1 and H4 while lowering GS7. Conversely, restricting top\-![][image81] (![][image84]) concentrates probability mass on dominant tokens, lowering H1 and H4 while increasing GS7. Grid-searching ![][image85] sampling combinations on validation generations identifies parameters that match target benchmark values (![][image86])1.

## **7\. Reproducibility Practices for Small-Scale Generative Music Experiments**

Evaluations of generative music models depend heavily on reproducible generation procedures34. Small variations in random seed initialization, GPU floating-point execution, or decoding parameters can alter generated outputs and yield inconsistent evaluation scores35.  
To ensure reproducibility, random seeds must be initialized across system libraries prior to model execution35:

Python  
import os  
import random  
import numpy as np  
import torch  
from transformers import set\_seed

def enforce\_strict\_reproducibility(seed: int \= 42):  
    random.seed(seed)  
    np.random.seed(seed)  
    torch.manual\_seed(seed)  
    torch.cuda.manual\_seed(seed)  
    torch.cuda.manual\_seed\_all(seed)  
    set\_seed(seed)  
      
    os.environ\["PYTHONHASHSEED"\] \= str(seed)  
    os.environ\["CUBLAS\_WORKSPACE\_CONFIG"\] \= ":4096:8"  
      
    torch.use\_deterministic\_algorithms(True, warn\_only=False)  
    torch.backends.cudnn.deterministic \= True  
    torch.backends.cudnn.benchmark \= False

enforce\_strict\_reproducibility(seed=42)

NVIDIA GPU execution introduces sources of non-determinism during parallel matrix operations35. Atomic addition operations (atomicAdd) in CUDA kernels execute floating-point operations in variable order across parallel threads, producing minor numerical variations in backward passes36. Setting CUBLAS\_WORKSPACE\_CONFIG=:4096:8 forces deterministic execution routines in cuBLAS libraries35.  
Calling Hugging Face model.generate(do\_sample=True) without an explicit PyTorch Generator instance relies on global CUDA random states, which can drift across evaluation calls35. Passing a thread-safe Generator initialized with a fixed seed (torch.Generator(device="cuda").manual\_seed(seed)) directly into generate() guarantees deterministic sampling35. Furthermore, because bfloat16 matrix operations can introduce minor low-order bit differences across GPU architectures (e.g., A100 vs. H200), validation runs should execute on unified hardware setups or use fp32 evaluation precision35.
